objective: Design climate-aware utility systems for residential buildings. Implement heating demand in cold climates, self-heating capabilities with explicit B2C fuel/electricity purchasing, and self-managed waste/water/sewage mechanics for off-grid buildings. Off-grid buildings MUST have a physical local water source (deep water well requiring CAPEX and maintenance) as an input before they can output sewage. Waste/sewage outputs local Pollution into the environment system (mass conservation). Ensure utility infrastructure (pipes, grids) physically connects parcels to utility networks. All utility pricing must use cost-plus models with CAPEX amortization and smoothed historical volumes.
constraints: RAM protection: cargo check and cargo clippy only
RBAC: no git checkout/switch/reset/rebase/clean
Rule 1: All utility payments must have strict counterparty (resident pays utility company); no fiat creation
Rule 2: Utility tariffs must scale by average_wage and consumption volume, not flat rates
Rule 3: Physical BOM for utility infrastructure must be static; financial costs from market prices
Rule 5: Utility capacity allocation must use market clearing or pro-rata by connected parcel demand
Rule 9: Parcel-to-utility-network linkage must use cadastre index lookups to avoid double mutable borrows
Rule 14: Extend existing utilities/ and energy/ modules; do not create parallel utility infrastructure
Rule 15: Utility consumption (heating, water, waste) must scale by floor_area, occupancy, and climate zone, not flat rates
Rule 16: Utility service sequencing must respect turn order: water well production → B2C fuel purchase → consumption → waste/pollution output → health impact
Rule 17: Utility access, quality, local pollution from off-grid waste, and well status must be visible in UI snapshots
Rule 19: Utility infrastructure must physically connect parcels to utility networks; no teleporting services. Disconnected parcels receive zero utility service.
Rule 20: Utility capacity and well yield must have hard limits with overflow (service degradation/rejection) behavior
Rule 21: Municipal utilities must use cost-plus pricing with CAPEX amortization and smoothed historical volumes (24-turn rolling averages)
Rule 22: Do not modify fertilizer, military, sports, or environment modules. Do NOT implement cooperative lifecycles — that is blueprint-007.
Rule 23: Surgically append to utilities/ and energy/ modules; do not overwrite existing utility structs
SCOPE LIMIT: This blueprint ONLY covers climate-aware utility systems (heating, water, waste, sewage) and their physical connection to residential parcels via infrastructure networks.

B2C FUEL PURCHASE: Residents in self-heating buildings MUST explicitly purchase fuel (Coal, Wood, Gas, or Electricity) on the retail market via B2C clearing BEFORE consuming for heat. Resident Labor account debited, fuel supplier (Company) credited. No fuel = no heat = health penalties. Fuel quantity = floor_area * climate_heating_degree_days * thermal_efficiency_coefficient.

MASS CONSERVATION — OFF-GRID WASTE/SEWAGE: Off-grid buildings' self-managed waste/sewage outputs local Pollution into the existing LocalPollutionState in environment/smog.rs. Waste_mass and sewage_volume (proportional to occupancy and floor_area) are converted to smog_level, water_pollution, and soil_contamination increases. Matter cannot disappear — it becomes pollution. Connected buildings route waste to municipal treatment (no pollution, pay fees). Trade-off: off-grid saves connection costs but generates pollution degrading ecological_health (blueprint-002) and harming health.

PHYSICAL WATER SOURCE — WELL REQUIREMENT (v6 rejection fix): Off-grid buildings CANNOT generate sewage_volume out of nowhere. Water must physically come from somewhere. Before an off-grid building can produce any sewage_volume, it MUST have a physical local water source: a deep water well (WaterWell) constructed on the parcel. The well has the following properties: (1) CAPEX: Construction requires physical inputs (Steel, Concrete, machinery) scaled by well_depth and aquifer_geology — no flat rates (Rule 15). (2) MAINTENANCE: Ongoing OPEX for pump maintenance, filter replacement, and energy (electricity or manual labor) scaled by water_volume_extracted. (3) YIELD: Well yield is physically limited by the local aquifer capacity in geography.rs — hard limit with depletion behavior (Rule 20). If the aquifer is depleted, the well runs dry and the building has NO water. (4) LIFECYCLE: Wells have complete lifecycle — construction, operation, depletion, and abandonment (Rule 4). (5) SEWAGE DEPENDENCY: sewage_volume = MIN(water_extracted_from_well, consumption_demand). If no well exists, or the well is dry, or the well cannot meet demand, sewage_volume is reduced proportionally — no water input means no sewage output. (6) The well must be explicitly linked to the parcel via cadastre. (7) Connected buildings use the municipal water grid instead (existing utilities/hydro_grid.rs) — no well needed. The well is ONLY for off-grid buildings. This respects the physics engine: water comes from the ground (aquifer), is consumed by residents, and exits as sewage/pollution. No water appears from thin air.
Use: bash .devin/scripts/request_integration.sh when done

completion_criteria: Climate-aware utilities implemented with self-heating capabilities. Residents explicitly purchase fuel via B2C retail clearing BEFORE consuming for heat. Off-grid buildings have physical water source (WaterWell with CAPEX, maintenance, aquifer-limited yield, complete lifecycle) — no well means no water means no sewage. Off-grid waste/sewage outputs local Pollution into environment/smog.rs (mass conservation). Connected buildings use municipal water grid and waste treatment. Utility infrastructure physically connects parcels to networks. All utility pricing uses cost-plus with CAPEX amortization. UI snapshots expose utility access, well status, and off-grid pollution contribution. M0 conservation maintained. Iron CI/CD green.
